title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and core operational processes for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees and contractors who require guidance on standard procedures, approval flows, and retained records.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, consultants, and third-party vendors with access to Redwood systems or data. Excludes team-level tactical runbooks (see team runbooks in eng-platform and eng-sre).

Principles (short)
------------------
- Least privilege: grant only the access required to perform the role.
- Auditability: approvals and changes must be traceable in our systems.
- Separation of duties: maintain independent review for financial and high-risk changes.
- Data protection by design: classify and protect data according to sensitivity.
- Vendor risk management: ensure security and contractual protections for third parties.

1) Access & Permissions
------------------------
Purpose: Define how access is requested, approved, provisioned, reviewed, and revoked across Redwood systems.

Key controls and processes:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default. Teams must define roles (owner, maintainer, reader) and map to system groups.
- Access request flow:
  1. Employee/contractor submits an access request using the Access Request Form (link: /confluence/templates/access-request-form).
  2. Requestor's manager and resource owner must approve via the identity platform (Okta) workflow.
  3. IT/Platform performs provisioning (within 24 business hours for standard requests).
- Onboarding: People Ops triggers baseline accounts and role assignments; engineering orgs complete system-specific access within 5 business days.
- Offboarding: People Ops initiates immediate revocation of all active credentials on termination/contract end. Team owners must confirm revocation in 24 hours.
- Periodic review: quarterly access reviews for all high-privilege groups (admins, production deployers, billing).
- MFA and SSO: enforced for all corporate accounts.
- Temporary elevated access: use time-bound sudo/access sessions (max 8 hours) with an approval ticket and post-action audit log.

Ownership:
- People Ops: account lifecycle and corporate access policy.
- Security: access controls, MFA enforcement, and audit logs.
- Team owners: define and approve team-level roles.

2) Change Management
--------------------
Purpose: Ensure controlled, auditable changes to production and critical infrastructure to reduce risk to availability and data integrity.

Change types and approval thresholds:
- Standard changes: pre-approved, low-risk, repeatable (e.g., routine config tweaks). Implement via scheduled windows and automated deployment pipelines.
- Minor changes: require team owner and SRE approval.
- Major changes: require RFC, cross-functional review, and change advisory board (CAB) approval. Major changes include schema migrations, major infra upgrades, and model rollout changes that impact latency or correctness.

Change process (recommended):
1. Create an RFC in the Change Management space using the RFC template. Include impact analysis, rollback plan, and test plan.
2. Run a staging deployment and a canary rollout for at least 24 hours (or as defined by the RFC).
3. Submit change for CAB review when classified as Major. CAB meets weekly; emergency CAB can be convened.
4. Authorize and schedule production deployment during approved maintenance windows (SLO-friendly times).
5. Execute, monitor, and validate post-deployment. Document metrics and incident indicators.
6. If any regression is detected, follow the rollback procedure immediately and file a post-change review.

Rollback and incident linkage:
- Every Major change must include a tested rollback procedure.
- If rollback occurs, a postmortem must be filed within 5 business days.

Tools and records:
- All approvals and RFCs must be recorded in the Confluence RFC template and linked to the change ticket in Jira.
- Deployment artifacts and logs stored in the CI system (GitHub Actions/ArgoCD).

3) Data Management
------------------
Purpose: Protect company and customer data through classification, retention, access controls, and operational safeguards.

Data classification:
- Public: information safe for public distribution.
- Internal: company-internal information; limited disclosure.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, or sensitive business data. Requires encryption at rest and in transit.
- Restricted: regulated data (HIPAA/PCI/other) requiring contractual and technical controls; special handling and logging.

Data handling requirements:
- Encryption: all Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Use company KMS for key management.
- Least privilege: production data queries require justification and manager approval; use anonymized or synthetic datasets for development where possible.
- Backups: daily backups for production datastores, retained per retention schedule below. Backups encrypted and stored in a separate account/region.
- Retention schedule (summary):
  - Logs (operational): 90 days default, extendable to 1 year for SRE investigations.
  - Backups: 30 days for dev/test, 90 days for production snapshots, 7 years for compliance-specific datasets when required.
  - Customer data retention: follow contractual terms; default 2 years unless otherwise specified.
- Data transfer: cross-border transfers require review by Security and Legal (related page: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).

Data access request and approval:
1. Submit Data Access Request (template link in Internal Templates).
2. Data owner reviews and approves with justification and scope.
3. Access provisioned with time-bound credentials and logged.

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Purpose: Provide a consistent, auditable procurement and expense process that balances speed with financial controls.

Approval matrix (summary table):
- <= $1,000: Manager approval (expense report or purchase order).
- $1,001 - $10,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- $10,001 - $50,000: Director + Finance approval and vendor risk review.
- > $50,000: VP-level approval, Legal review, and procurement lead involvement.

Procurement process:
1. Raise a purchase request in the Procurement system (link: /confluence/templates/purchase-request). Include business case, preferred vendor, and budget code.
2. Finance validates budget and issues a PO for approved purchases.
3. Vendor on-boarding must be completed for purchases > $10,000 (see Vendor Management).
4. Receipt and invoice submission: submit invoices to AP within 5 business days of receipt.
5. Expense reimbursements: submit via Expense system with receipts within 30 days; manager approval required.

Corporate cards:
- Issued to employees with travel or purchasing responsibilities. Monthly card reconciliations required.
- Card limit set by role; exceptions via Finance approval.

Travel policy (summary)
----------------------
Purpose: Define acceptable travel spending, pre-approval requirements, and reimbursement flows.

- Pre-approval: All travel with cost > $500 requires manager pre-approval. Out-of-country travel requires People Ops and Security notification for traveler safety checks.
- Booking: Use company travel portal for flights and hotels; book economy or equivalent unless pre-approved class is justified.
- Per diem: Meals and incidental allowance follows published per-diem table (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/travel-per-diem-table).
- Reimbursable expenses: airfare, lodging, ground transport, work-related meals, work visas, and necessary vaccinations. Non-reimbursable: alcohol (unless business entertainment pre-approved), personal excursions, upgrades without approval.
- Expense reports: submit within 15 days of return with itemized receipts. Finance will flag exceptions.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Purpose: Standardize supplier onboarding, security evaluation, contract terms, and ongoing oversight.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Initial procurement request and business justification.
- Vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire) completed by Security.
- Contract and SLA review by Legal (include data handling and termination clauses).
- Insurance and business continuity checks for critical vendors.
- Add to vendor registry and schedule periodic review (annually for critical vendors, biennial for others).

Vendor performance and SLAs:
- Define measurable SLAs in the contract (uptime, response time, incident response).
- Finance/Procurement owner monitors spend vs. contract and enforces renewal/cancellation timelines.

Offboarding vendors:
- Terminate access to systems, retrieve company data, and confirm data destruction as contractually required.
- Retain final contracts and termination evidence in the vendor registry.

6) Internal Templates & Links
----------------------------
Standard templates (all available in Templates library):
- Access Request Form: /confluence/templates/access-request-form
- RFC / Change Request template: /confluence/templates/rfc-template
- Purchase Request template: /confluence/templates/purchase-request
- Data Access Request template: /confluence/templates/data-access-request
- Travel Expense form: /confluence/templates/travel-expense-form
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: /confluence/templates/vendor-security-questionnaire

7) Exception and Escalation Process
------------------------------------
- Exceptions to policy require a formal exception request submitted to Security or People Ops depending on policy scope. Exceptions are time-bound and must include compensating controls.
- Escalation matrix: manager -> director -> VP -> Risk Committee for unresolved high-risk items.

8) Review cadence and ownership
--------------------------------
- This company-wide policy document is owned by People Ops. Security, Finance, and Legal are co-owners for their sections.
- Full policy review: annual.
- Quarterly operational check-ins: People Ops, Security, Finance.

Appendix: Contacts and resources
--------------------------------
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Security (questions and vendor security reviews): security@redwood.com
- Finance & Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Change Advisory Board (CAB) chair: cab@redwood.com
- Templates library: /confluence/templates

Change log (high level)
-----------------------
- 2026-03-04: Initial consolidated policy created.
- 2026-07-10: Added temporary elevated access guidance and clarified backup retention.
- 2026-12-16: Updated procurement thresholds, clarified travel pre-approval rules, and added vendor offboarding steps.

If you have questions about how these policies apply to your team or need assistance with templates, contact People Ops or the relevant policy owner listed above.
